This case is heard finally with the consent of learned counsel for the parties.
Accordingly, I.A. No.3957 of 2025 , which is an application for suspension of sentence and grant of bail to the appellant, is dismissed as withdrawn.

This appeal is filed by the appellant being aggrieved of the judgment dated 30.01.2025 passed by the learned Additional Sessions Judge, Parasiya, District Chhindwara in S.C. No. 26/2022 whereby the appellant has been NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2025:MPHC-JBP:43117 2 CRA-1858-2025 convicted under Section 363 of IPC and sentenced to 3 years' R.I. with fine of Rs.1,000/-, Section 366-A of IPC and sentenced to R.I. for 05 years with fine of Rs.1,000/- and also under Section 5(L)/6 of the POCSO Act and sentenced to R.I. for 20 years with fine of Rs.1,000/- along with default stipulations.

sentences.text: Though appellant has also been convicted under Section 376(2) (N) of IPC, but has not been sentenced separately.
2. Learned counsel for the appellant submits that it is a case of consent where the victim had gone with the appellant on her own volition.

Reading from the 164 Cr.P.C. statement of the victim, it is pointed out that she admitted knowing the appellant for the last eight months and also being in love relationship with the appellant Raja @ Gajendra.
She also admitted in her statement that Raja had established physical relationship with her consent.

Thus, it is pointed out that the only issue which is required to be seen is whether the victim was adult at the time of the incident or not ?
3.
It is pointed out that the date of birth of the victim in school record is mentioned as 8.1.2004 and the incident is of 16.11.2021.

It is submitted that P.W.4 school teacher, who has produced the Dakhil Kharij Register (Ex.P/7C ) has admitted that the victim was given admission in the sixth class and her date of birth is recorded on the basis of T.C. but that Transfer Certificate issued by the so-called primary school was not produced before the school where the victim was given admission in the sixth class.

It is pointed out that prosecution has not produced Dakhil Kharij register of Class I of the victim and when neither T.C. has been produced nor Dakhil Kharij Register of the first class then it cannot be said that the prosecution has NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2025:MPHC-JBP:43117 3 CRA-1858-2025
proved the age of the victim beyond reasonable doubt.

4. It is also submitted that in fact mother of the victim (P.W.1) admitted that her marriage was performed when she was 16 years of age, then she stated that victim was born 10 years after her marriage, therefore, it is evident that when victim was born, at that time age of the mother was 26 years whereas she has shown her age in the deposition to be 45 years, therefore, as per the statement of P.W.1 also the victim was adult at the time of the incident.
5. Ms. Shweta Yadav, learned Dy. Advocate General submitted that as per the tenth class marksheet available on record as Ex. P/14, date of birth of the victim is mentioned as 8.1.2004.

6. After hearing learned counsel for the parties and going through the record, as far as date mentioned in the tenth class marksheet is concerned, it has lost sanctity, but in view of the evidence of P.W.4 Shri Ujjwal Pethe, primary teacher, it is evident that he has admitted that he is posted in Middle School, Aptara from 21.07.2010 till date.
He admitted that whatever information is recorded in Ex. P/7, was not recorded in front of him.

He has admitted that he cannot say as to how that information was recorded, then on his own he stated that the date of birth was recorded on the basis of T.C. of the primary school but further admitted that Transfer Certificate of the primary school is not available on record.

Thus, tenth class mark-sheet recording the date of birth on the basis of school admission in the sixth class cannot be said to be sacrosanct, especially when the victim studied from Class Ist to V th and the prosecution did not deem it proper to produce Dakhil NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2025:MPHC-JBP:43117 4 CRA-1858-2025 Kharij from the school which was first attended by the victim.
7. As far as mother of the victim (P.W.1) is concerned, she has admitted in paragraph 3 of her cross-examination that when she was 16 years of age, at that time her marriage was performed.

sentences.text: After two years of marriage, eldest daughter was born and then she stated that victim, who is fifth number child was born ten years after marriage.

When this chronology is taken into consideration then at the time of deposition of P.W.1,
victim was 19 years of age, thus when the incident took place on 16.11.2021 she was more than 18 years of age.
8. P.W.2 victim too has admitted in paragraph 3 that at the time of the incident she was 18 years of age and, therefore, she had entered into a wedlock.
She stated that she has a younger brother and elder sisters, who all are married.
She further admitted that her husband is a resident of Harai.
He has a fourteen years old daughter from his first marriage.
He performed second marriage with the victim.
She also admitted that when her marriage was performed she was more than 18 years of age.
9. When all these facts are taken into consideration along with the evidence of Dr. Shashi Atulkar (P.W.6), who admitted that there were no injury marks on the body of the victim.
There were no signs of struggle.
She admitted that she had mentioned age of the victim on the basis of estimation and there can be a difference of one to one and a half years in her estimation.
Another prosecution witness P.W.3, who is friend of the victim has admitted that at the time of the incident, age of the victim was 19 years because she is one year younger to this witness.
She stated that though victim NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2025:MPHC-JBP:43117 5 CRA-1858-2025 was not having admission in the college, yet she was travelling with them to the college.

Thus, it is evident that the prosecution has failed to prove the age of victim to be minor at the time of the incident, therefore, positivity of DNA sample is not a sufficient circumstance to uphold conviction.
10. Accordingly, this appeal is allowed.
The impugned judgment of conviction is hereby set aside.
Appellant is acquitted of the charges.
Appellant be released immediately, if not required in any other case.
11. Case property be disposed of as per the directions of the learned trial Court.
12. Record of the Trial Court be sent back immediately.
